title: 555 astable LED flasher
goal: Reads like a textbook schematic: IC pins on the correct sides, power at the top, ground at the bottom, no line crossing a component body.

rubric.must: No wire passes through the inside of a component symbol or the IC rectangle.
The supply rail is drawn above the circuit and ground below it, following schematic convention.
IC pins leave the chip body on a side consistent with their function; no pin stub is drawn inside the body.
Each component's reference designator and value sits beside its own symbol, not overlapping a neighbour's.
Wires run horizontally or vertically, with corners rather than diagonals.
No two pieces of text overlap, and no text is crossed by a wire.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex, which preferred its own SVG over the generated picture. Checked against the netlist: all eight 555 pins land where the DSL puts them, and every value matches (BAT1 9 V, R1 10 kΩ, R2 100 kΩ, C1 10 µF, C2 10 nF, R3 470 Ω).

audit.reviewedBy: a practising electronics engineer checking a schematic before layout

findings.what: U1 has no supply decoupling capacitor between pin 8 and pin 1.
findings.why: A bipolar 555 draws brief switching-current spikes that can disturb the supply and cause false triggering, especially with battery leads. C2 bypasses CTRL and does not provide supply decoupling. The [TI datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ne555.pdf) recommends 100 nF across the supply.
findings.fix: Add a 100 nF ceramic capacitor rated at least 16 V directly between pins 8 and 1, placed close to U1 with short connections.
